Keywords: Order vows of poverty chastity and obedience
RagShortTexts: Professed brethren follow vows and communal discipline.
Personal poverty can coexist with the Order’s property.

Variants.Content: Professed brethren bind themselves to poverty, chastity and obedience under communal arrangements. Houses still manage land, provisions and equipment. Visitors and employees have different status; shared belief requires daily organization to sustain service.
A brother accounts for issued equipment and distinguishes damage from private taking. Reporting sick horses or shortages enables repair rather than undermining obedience.
Estate revenues must reach the house. Vows cannot deliver carts; discipline distinguishes neglect, accident and shortage to avoid producing concealed problems.
Paid workers need food and wages without sharing lifelong vows. Estates and workshops depend on them; neglecting costs interrupts the house’s daily supplies.
